doc.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

chapter: Following the drum to New York
title: Ancestral calling to leave Trinidad for New York
summary: Spiritual awakenings told him to leave his jobs; he left for New York on May 15, 1984.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Was the spirituality that you talked about yesterday that’s connected to this percussive music, was that spirituality a part of your life at that point?

Yes, yes. My desire to leave Trinidad and follow the path of the drum was actually prompted by my ancestral awakenings. They are the ones who told me you must leave Trinidad. You cannot do what you have to do here. You must leave and you must follow the sound of the drum. Monk, I left one of the biggest paying jobs for a young scientist. I left one of the highest paying seats in the music world in our small island. I packed my bags. My parents thought that I was crazy. “Son, where are you going?” “I’m going to New York.” “What you gonna do?” “I don’t know but I want to play music.” “How are you gonna live?” “I don’t know but I will find a way.” I left the island on May 15, 1984. It was a full moon. To be in New York on May 16, which was my birthday. I would turn 27 I believe, to start a new life. And that’s how I came. I came — I had to jump. I had to jump and I had to find my wings. And if this spiritual calling was going to be as great as I had experienced it in my time in Trinidad and growing up etcetera, then I knew that it would provide me with the wings and the courage and the sustenance to be able to do what I had to do.
